title: CRLA/149/2012 of SHRAWAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL

Criminal Appeal No. 149 of 2012
Shrawan,S/o Nortu
R/o Village Sarthedi Shahajanpur
Thana Bhagwanpur, District Haridwar
Ö..Ö Appellant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand through its secretary, Home Dehradun
 ÖÖÖÖ. Respondent
Mr. S.S. Bhandari, Advocate, present for the appellant
Mr. Aasif Ali, Brief Holder, present for the State.
Honʹble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
This appeal, preferred under section 374 of
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short Cr.P.C.)
is directed against the judgment and order dated
08.05.2012 passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Roorkee, in Sessions Trial No. 123 of 2011, whereby
said court has convicted accused/appellant Shrawan
under section 363, 366 and 376 IPC. The accused/
appellant Shrawan has been sentenced to rigorous
imprisonment for a period of three years and directed
to pay fine ` 1,000/- under section 363 IPC, rigorous
imprisonment for a period of five years and directed
to pay fine of ` 2,000/- under section 366 IPC and
rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years

2
and directed to pay fine of 3,000/- under section 376
IPC.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the lower court record.
3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that P.W.2 Soni is
daughter of P.W.1 Meghraj of village Sarthedi
Shahajanpur of District Haridwar. On 15.08.2010
P.W.1 Meghraj gave a report (Ex. A1) at Police Station
Bhagwanpur that his daughter Soni was missing from
the preceding night. And from the same night
accused Shrawan son of Nortu was also missing. A
case was registered at the police station and both the
boy and girl were apprehended by P.W.4 Sub-
Inspector Dinesh Chand Gupta and P.W.5 Station
Officer Jawahar lal on 17.08.2010 at 6:15 p.m., from
railway station Tejupur. Thereafter they were
interrogated, and the girl was produced before P.W.3
Dr. Deepa on 18.08.2010 for her medical examination.
After medical examination said medical officer
prepared her report (Ex. A2) and observed that there
was no injury on the person of the girl. As to the
determination of age P.W.3 Dr. Deepa advised
radiological examination, and after receiving
radiological report she prepared supplementary

3
report (Ex. A3) opining that the girl was aged more
than eighteen years. She further observed in her
supplementary report that on pathological
examination of slides of smear of the girl, no
spermatozoa dead or alive were seen. According to
prosecution case thereafter the girl (P.W.2) Soni was
taken to the Judicial Magistrate, Roorkee, on
23.08.2012 where she did not allege anything against
the accused, and simply stated that she wanted to go
home (as such the girl made no allegation of
kidnapping or rape against the accused even at the
stage of recording of statement under section 164
Cr.P.C.). It appears that crime no. 215 of 2010 was
registered under section 363, 366 and 376 IPC against
the accused by the police on 15.08.2010, on the basis
of report (Ex. A1) lodged by P.W.1 Meghraj (father of
the girl) and after investigation, Sub Inspector Nawab
Singh, Investigating Officer (P.W.6) filed charge sheet
against accused Shrawan for his trial in respect of
offences punishable under section 363, 366 and 376
IPC.
4. On receipt of the charge sheet the Judicial
Magistrate, after giving necessary copies to the
accused as required under section 207 Cr.P.C.
committed the case to the court of Sessions for trial.

4
On 27.07.2011, learned Sessions Judge, Haridwar,
after hearing the parties framed charge of offences
punishable under section 363, 366 and 376 IPC against
accused Shrawan who pleaded not guilty and claimed
to be tried. It appears that for further trial the case
was transferred to the court of Additional Sessions
Judge, Roorkee, where P.W.1 Meghraj , P.W.2 Soni
(victim), P.W.3 Dr. Deepa (medical officer who
medically examined the girl), P.W.4 Sub Inspector
Dinesh Chand Gupta (witness of recovery of the girl),
P.W.5 Sr. Sub Inspector Jawahar Lal (who was also
witness of the recovery of the girl), P.W.6 Sub
Inspector Nawab Singh (Investigating Officer) and
P.W.7 Head Constable Rajendra Singh (who prepared
the check report of FIR) were examined.
5. Oral and documentary evidence was put to the
accused under section 313 Cr.P.C. in reply to which
the accused pleaded that the evidence adduced
against him was false however he admitted that when
he was going to Yamuna Nagar, Soni (P.W.2) met him
and after he made her to talk to her parents, she went
with him. He further stated that he thought the girl
had taken consent of her parents to go with him. In
defence D.W.1 Shakeel Ahmad and D.W.2

5
Dharamveer were examined. D.W.2 has stated that
after the accused and the girl (Soni) came to his house
on 15.08.2010, he also made the girl to talk to her
parents on phone.
6. The trial court after hearing the parties found the
accused Shrawan guilty of charge of offences
punishable under section 363, 366 and 376 IPC. After
hearing the parties on sentence, the trial court has
sentenced the convict to rigorous imprisonment for a
period of three years and directed to pay fine of `
1,000/- under section 363 IPC, rigorous imprisonment
for a period of five years and directed to pay fine of `
2,000/- under section 366 IPC and rigorous
imprisonment for a period of seven years and
directed to pay fine of ` 3,000/- under section 376 IPC.
Aggrieved by said judgment and order dated
08.05.2012 this appeal was filed by the convict.
7. Before further discussion this Court thinks it just
and proper to mention the observations made by
P.W.3 Dr. Deepa who medically examined the girl on
18.08.2010. The observations made by said medical
officer in her report (Ex. A2) are being reproduced
below:-

6
ìOn examination_ General condition normal, average
built axillary and pubic hair of normal growth, breast
well developed.
Injuries-_ No injuries including private parts seen.
Per Vaginum- P/V admits one finger easily, hymen
ruptured, no bleeding P/V seen, uterus normal in
size, UPT negative.
Vaginal smear taken and sent for histopatholigcal
examination of any spermatozoa dead or alive.
Adv.- Plain x-ray right elbow, knee and wrist joint
for confirmation of age
8. P.W.3 Dr. Deepa in her supplementary report
dated 28.03.2010, on receipt of the pathological and
radiological report, has made following observations
in Ex. A3:-
i. On the basis of radiological finding, age of Km.
Soni is more than eighteen years.
ii. Vagina smear examination report- No
spermatozoa seen dead or alive.
9. It is relevant to mention here that P.W.6 S.I.
Nawab Singh (Investigating Officer) has stated that
on 23.08.2010 the girl was produced before the
Magistrate for her examination to be recorded under
section 164 Cr.P.C. Page no. 11A/1 is the

7
memorandum prepared by Judicial Magistrate,
Roorkee, after the girl (Soni) was produced before
him for recording statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.
In said document the girl simply told the Magistrate
that she wants to go home and she does not want to
say anything. In other words, it can be said that Km.
Soni did not made any allegation against accused
Shrawan before the Magistrate when she was
produced for recording of her statement under
section 164 Cr.P.C.
10. P.W.1 Meghraj has simply stated that on
14.08.2010 his daughter Sonia (Soni) was sleeping in
the night but on the next morning she was found
missing. He further told that one Shakeel of his
village told him that his daughter was seen going all
alone near the plot of one Idrish. P.W.1 Meghraj
further told that from the very day accused Shrawan
son of Nortu was also missing from the village. This
witness proved FIR (Ex. A1) lodged by him at police
station Bhagwanpur.
11. P.W.2 Soni is the star witness of this case who
has supported the prosecution case, and told that she
was taken away on a motor-cycle by accused Shrawan

8
when she was coming back after easing out herself in
the jungle. She further told that accused committed
rape on her. She disclosed that she was taken to
Dehradun where she remained in a rented
accommodation for three days with the accused.
However, the girl failed to disclose as to why she did
not raise any alarm when she was taken by accused
Shrawan on way to Dehradun or after reaching
Dehradun. She has candidly admitted in her cross-
examination that she did not shout for help
anywhere. She further admitted in her cross-
examination that she did not raise any hue and cry
when she lived with accused in Dehradun. The most
relevant portion in her cross-examination which
suggests that P.W.2 Soni might have gone with the
accused on her own volition is reproduced below:-
ìgekjs xkao ds cgkj jksgkydh dk nw/kokyk 'kdhy feyk Fkk ftls
ns[kdj blus oaccused) eq>s eksVj lkbfdy ls mrkj fn;k Fkk

(Shakeel of village Bahar Rohalki met us on
which I was made get down by the accused who
asked me to follow him and he was going
ahead).
12. On careful examination of the statement of the
girl P.W.2 Soni, keeping in mind her age and her

9
relation with the accused as reflects from the record,
this Court is of the view that it cannot be ruled out
that the girl had gone on her own volition with
accused Shrawan, and consensual sex between the
two cannot be ruled out. That being so it cannot be
said that the charge of offences punishable under
section 363, 366 or 376 IPC is proved beyond
reasonable doubt against accused Shrawan son of
Nortu.
13. For the reasons as discussed above, this appeal
deserves to be allowed. Accordingly, the appeal is
allowed. Conviction and sentence recorded by the
learned Additional Sessions Judge, Roorkee, under
section 363, 366 and 376 IPC against accused Shrawan
(in Sessions Trial No. 123 of 2011) is hereby set aside.
Accused/appellant Shrawan is acquitted of the charge
of offences punishable under section 363, 363 and 376
IPC. He is on bail. He need not surrender. Lower
court record be sent back.
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Parul 23.05.2013
